_status: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED (wired automatically by the gen-slices auto-loader).
_note: Third round of 2026-08-28. Closes the gap the EU national-chains round left open that morning: every EU country except Germany had an `*-edp-inventory` node — the Article 9 methods document Regulation 479/2009 compels — wired to the regulation and to ESA 2010 but to NO NATIONAL DATA AT ALL. Germany was the only country with real deficit/debt release nodes (`de-destatis-debt-annual`, `de-destatis-debt-quarterly`), so it was used as the template. This slice gives twelve more countries the national data end: 12 nodes, 36 edges. LANDED FOR: AT (two nodes — deficit and debt are separate Maastricht-indicator releases), BE, IE, FI, SE, LV, PL, HU, SK, HR, GR. NOT LANDED, and the reasons are in `_dropped`: ES, PT, BG, MT, LT, EE, CY, RO, SI. NEGATIVE METHOD FINDING WORTH MORE THAN SOME OF THE EDGES: the Eurostat per-country government-finance metadata URL pattern `gov_10dd_edpt1_esms_<cc>.htm` — the obvious analogue of the HICP and LFS patterns that made the morning's EU round cheap — **404s for every country tried** (bg, ro, el, cy, mt, pl, hu, sk, si, hr), as does the `gov_10dd_esms_<cc>.htm` variant. Only the non-country-specific `gov_10dd_esms.htm` exists. Do not plan a round around it. What works instead is the NSI's own EDP release page, which in most countries states the notification obligation in quotable terms. FOUR PROPOSED COUNTRIES WERE REJECTED AT MINT TIME ON EVIDENCE QUALITY, not availability: Bulgaria and Malta rested on a page TITLE and a homepage listing respectively (PLAYBOOK rule 16 — a page title is not evidence), Lithuania's page carried no EDP, ESA or Regulation language at all, and Spain's rested on an INE catalogue record for a Banco de España series plus an inference. Estonia was rejected after the orchestrating session re-fetched its release and confirmed the agent's proposed basis did not hold — the page contains no EDP, Eurostat or ESA 2010 language whatever, only a definitional use of 'Maastricht debt'. Poland went the other way: re-fetching found the page says considerably MORE than the agent reported, including the operative sentence naming the transmission itself.

reports.title: Öffentliches Defizit / Öffentlicher Überschuss — General government deficit/surplus (Maastricht-Indikatoren)
reports.description: Austria's Maastricht-indicator release on the general government deficit and surplus. Statistik Austria states "Für die budgetäre Notifikation an die Europäische Kommission berechnete Statistik Austria die Daten" (Statistik Austria calculates the data for the budgetary notification to the European Commission), compiled "gemäß ESVG 2010".
reports.cadence_note: Twice yearly on the EDP notification cycle; the page's listed next-publication dates were 30.09.2026 and 31.03.2027.

reports.title: Öffentlicher Schuldenstand — General government debt (Maastricht-Indikatoren)
reports.description: Austria's quarterly general government debt release, the debt half of the Maastricht indicators. Statistik Austria states the debt is compiled "gemäß den Kategorien des Europäischen Systems Volkswirtschaftlicher Gesamtrechnungen (ESVG 2010)", under the heading "Vierteljährlicher öffentlicher Schuldenstand". Kept as a second Austrian node because Austria publishes deficit and debt as genuinely separate releases on different cadences — the same annual/quarterly split Germany already has in this corpus.
reports.cadence_note: Quarterly; the fetched page's current figure was labelled 2026 Q1, with further releases scheduled 30.09.2026, 30.12.2026, 31.03.2027 and 30.06.2027.

reports.title: Notification EDP — Déficit et dette des administrations publiques (EDP notification: Belgium's general government deficit and debt)
reports.publisher: Institut des Comptes Nationaux / Instituut voor de Nationale Rekeningen (ICN/INR), with the National Bank of Belgium
reports.description: The clearest statement of the EDP mechanism found in this round: "On 20 April 2026, the National Accounts Institute (INR) is releasing the tables drawn up to notify Belgium's general government deficit and debt to the European Commission in accordance with the excessive deficit procedure (EDP)," compiled "in accordance with the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010)."
reports.cadence_note: The document states it directly: "This notification is made twice a year, in April and October."

reports.title: Government Finance Statistics (Annual)
reports.description: Ireland's annual government finance statistics release. The CSO states "Government accounts are compiled in the EU according to the European System of National Accounts 2010 (ESA2010) framework" and that "The main EDP notification tables for Ireland will be published on 22nd April 2026, the same day as the Eurostat release of EDP statistics." NOTE, and it is an unusually candid one: the same page warns that "Annual Government Finance Statistics are benchmarked to the most recent EDP notification and so may not be fully aligned with the Annual National Accounts and related publications" — which is why no edge was minted from this node to ie-cso-national-accounts. The publisher itself flags the two may disagree.
reports.cadence_note: Two vintages a year of the same annual reference-year data, on the EDP cycle — separate editions exist titled "Government Finance Statistics 2024 (April 2025)" and "Government Finance Statistics 2024 (October 2025)". CSO also runs a distinct quarterly GFS(Q) series, confirmed to exist but never fetched, so it was not minted.

reports.title: Julkisen talouden alijäämä ja velka — General government deficit and debt
reports.description: Statistics Finland's dedicated EDP statistic (code 'jali'): "These statistics contain data on the deficit and debt of government finance in Finland," and "Member states report EDP deficits and debts to the EU Commission twice yearly for assessment under the Stability and Growth Pact." Finland is the only country in this round whose publisher explicitly ties the EDP deficit to the national accounts concept: "General government deficit also called EDP deficit (= Excessive Deficit Procedure), corresponds with the general government net lending/borrowing in the national accounts."
reports.cadence_note: Twice yearly — preliminary figures in April and final figures in October, matching the EU's end-March / end-September EDP notification deadlines.

reports.title: Utgiftsprocedur vid alltför stora underskott — Excessive Deficit Procedure: general government net lending/borrowing and consolidated gross debt
reports.description: SCB's EDP release: "The statistics show general government net lending/net borrowing and gross debt according to the rules in the Stability and Growth Pact," and "The calculations for the Excessive Deficit Procedure are submitted by Statistics Sweden to Eurostat in accordance with the EU Stability and Growth Pact under Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009." No ESA 2010 statement was found on SCB's English pages, so unlike most countries here this node carries no esa-2010 edge — see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: INFERRED, not quoted: statistical-news releases were observed roughly six months apart (a 2026-09-30 next-publishing date following a 2026-03-31 release; the same pattern in 2021), consistent with the EU's twice-yearly EDP cycle, but no fetched SCB page said 'twice a year' in so many words.

reports.title: Vispārējās valdības budžeta deficīta un parāda notifikācija — Notification on General Government Budget Deficit and Debt
reports.publisher: Centrālā statistikas pārvalde (CSP) / Central Statistical Bureau of Latvia

_dropped.edge: gov_10dd_edpt1_esms_<cc>.htm — the Eurostat per-country government-finance metadata pattern
_dropped.why: METHOD FINDING, and the most useful thing in this file. The morning's EU round was made cheap by two Eurostat per-country metadata URL patterns (`prc_hicp_esmshi4_<cc>.htm`, `employ_simslfs_<cc>.htm`). The obvious government-finance analogue DOES NOT EXIST: `gov_10dd_edpt1_esms_<cc>.htm` returned 404 for every country tried across two independent agents — bg, ro, el, cy, mt, pl, hu, sk, si, hr — as did the `gov_10dd_esms_<cc>.htm` variant. Only the non-country-specific `gov_10dd_esms.htm` exists, and it carries only a generic 'Member States compile and report this data to Eurostat' line with no per-country annexes in the fetched extract. Do not scope a future round around this pattern. What works instead is the NSI's own EDP release page, which in 11 of 20 countries states the notification obligation in directly quotable terms.

REJECTED AT MINT TIME ON EVIDENCE QUALITY. Spain's actual EDP compiler page — IGAE, at igae.pap.hacienda.gob.es — returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED and was not worked around. The agent fell back to INE's statistical-operation catalogue record (Ficha IOE nº 37144) for a Banco de España series, 'Deuda Pública según el Protocolo de Déficit Excesivo', which does give a real title and 'Periodicidad de la difusión: Trimestral'. But a catalogue record is not the release, the record contains no ESA 2010 statement, and the proposed edges rested on inferring the EDP link from the operation's title plus its citation of Regulation 3605/93. Under this project's rules that is an inference, not a documented dependency. LEAD: retry IGAE on a different day, or find Banco de España's own page for the series rather than INE's catalogue entry for it.

UNREACHABLE, for the third time today. Every ine.pt URL attempted failed with a robots.txt fetch error (SSL certificate failure / connection timeout on robots.txt itself), as did gee.gov.pt, a Portuguese government economic office page citing INE's PDE release. This is the same ine.pt failure mode that cost Portugal its LFS node and left pt-ine-idef pointing at the IPC release in the morning's EU round, and it has now been reproduced independently by three separate agents and the orchestrating session. It reads as an infrastructure fault on the Portuguese government domains from this fetch environment rather than a deliberate disallow — but it was not worked around. Portugal is now the single most under-served EU country in this corpus.

PLAYBOOK rule 16 — a page title is not evidence. The NSI page (nsi.bg/en/content/2431/...) does load and is genuinely Bulgaria's government finance page, so this is a cheap retry: fetch it again and look for an ESA 2010 or Regulation 479/2009 sentence in the body, or find NSI's EDP press release.

REJECTED AT MINT TIME for the same reason as Bulgaria, compounded: the proposed node's url was NSO Malta's HOMEPAGE (nso.gov.mt), not the release, and the evidence was the homepage's listing of 'Government Debt and Deficit under the Maastricht Treaty 2025' plus its headline figures. The release plainly exists and is well named — this is the cheapest retry in this file. Fetch the release page itself and the node is mintable with an ESA 2010 edge as well.

REJECTED AT MINT TIME. The one Lithuanian page reached (osp.stat.gov.lt/en/valdzios-sektoriaus-finansai1) is a general 'General government finance' overview presenting deficit and debt figures and the Maastricht 60%-of-GDP criterion, with NO excessive-deficit-procedure, ESA 2010 or Regulation 479/2009 language anywhere on it — the agent said so itself. REJECTED AT MINT TIME AFTER AN INDEPENDENT RE-FETCH, which is the reason to keep this entry. The agent proposed the edge on the release's use of 'Maastricht debt' terminology, arguing it 'ties it directly' to the EDP. The orchestrating session re-fetched the page (stat.ee/en/news/general-government-debt-continued-grow-2024-...) and confirmed the opposite: it contains NO sentence mentioning the excessive deficit procedure, notification to Eurostat or the European Commission, or ESA 2010. The single Maastricht reference is definitional — 'General government debt, or Maastricht debt, refers to the liabilities of the general government units in the following categories: currency and deposits, debt securities and loans.' That is a glossary line, not a statement of the EDP relationship. Estonia needs a dedicated EDP-notification page; the news release is not it.

A guessed subject-page URL 404'd. Cyprus's Ministry of Finance was never tried and is the obvious next place to look, since in several EU countries the finance ministry rather than the NSI fronts the EDP release.

insse.ro returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED again, exactly as it did in the morning's EU round where it cost Romania its IAPC node. An earlier insse.ro homepage fetch loaded but showed no government-finance section. Romania's Ministry of Finance (mfinante.gov.ro) was never attempted before the budget ran out and is the better target — Romania's EDP notification is co-compiled with the ministry.

SURS's stat.si returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED on all three URLs tried (main news page, topic index, and the methodological-note PDF at StatWeb/File/DocSysFile/10165) — the same domain that partly blocked Slovenia in the morning's EU round, where its CPI methodological note DID load. So stat.si is selectively rather than wholly unreachable and is worth retrying on specific document paths. Untried alternatives: gov.si, and SURS's PxWeb data portal.

NOT AN OVERSIGHT — the publisher warns against it. The CSO states "Annual Government Finance Statistics are benchmarked to the most recent EDP notification and so may not be fully aligned with the Annual National Accounts and related publications." That is an explicit caution that the two series can disagree, which is the opposite of a data dependency. Contrast Finland, where Statistics Finland states the EDP deficit "corresponds with the general government net lending/borrowing in the national accounts" and the edge WAS minted. Two publishers, two genuinely different relationships — worth preserving as a data point about how much this varies.
